shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index gained on Friday as capesize vessel rates strengthened, but the benchmark still posted a weekly loss.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index gained on Friday as capesize vessel rates strengthened, but the benchmark still posted a weekly loss.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, rose 34 points, or 1%, to 3,370 points. However, the index was down nearly 4% for the week so far.
The capesize index (.BACI) rose 112 points, or 2%, to 5,768 points. It was on track for a weekly fall of 5%.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, increased by $1,019 to $48,812.

Iron ore prices rose for a third straight session, supported by higher-than-expected hot metal output. Lingering demand uncertainty, swelling portside inventory and thin steel margins kept prices on track for a second weekly loss.
Meanwhile, the panamax index (.BPNI) fell 31 points, or 1.4%, to 2,251 points, and was headed for a weekly drop of 6.5%.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, fell $273 to $20,262.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index (.BSIS) inched up 5 points, or 0.3%, at 1,767. The index recorded a weekly gain of 2.8% so far.

title: Baltic index rises on stronger capesize vessel rates, but posts weekly decline
